The scope exclusions separately name browser paid fate transactions but do not clearly exclude ordinary browser Stage. Thus the proposed factory/refusal contract does not unambiguously distinguish an ordinary browser invocation from actual recorder/recovery ownership. This is an eligibility-contract defect/ambiguity in the proposed design, not proof of an existing runtime regression.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Actual fate behavior and separate action owners
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Accurate. Reuse predicate remains permissive; null array throws outside parse catch. Valid existing state preserves lock/timestamp/gacha fields and references, with no application write/RNG. Fresh success is20 visible+4 hidden Fill calls with the original modulo/threshold/emptyDiceUsed behavior. Reveal/Rewrite/Rotate and fee owners are separate. Explorer can call GetOrCreate before fee deduction; the proposal does not authorize replaying those actions.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Same final read witness rather than reread reconstruction
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Accurate proposed seam. Existing public text read recovers, decodes a selected byte snapshot, calls after-read hook and may reacquire/reread. A second independent read or reserialization is not the original byte witness. The additive seam must retain the actual final selected snapshot and the exact decoded text while preserving the same follow-up behavior. PF-P02/P03 correctly remain unqualified; no completed-read claim is permitted at a cut where an original follow-up remains unissued.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Per-slot entropy, clock and seal safety
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Conditionally coherent. Gate then frame-state lock, no RNG/I/O/clock/await under locks; once-only four-byte slot registration and retained returned value before borrow release. Seal allows the already-armed slot to finish, forbids the next unissued slot, and cannot classify a changed failed buffer as a draw. Materialized creation/write clock results and desired bytes are retained once. Discarded constructor-clock defaults are acknowledged as technical work, not omitted domain timestamps. Actual registration/supervisor APIs and surviving thread/task custody are prerequisites, not demonstrated source capabilities.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Source before-image and publication outcomes
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Accurate distinction. Current ordinary publication rereads its before image; proposed exact earlier-read baseline is an explicit additive guard, not a claimed existing guarantee. Native publisher compares expected before bytes and retains Committed before cleanup. Directory preparation, mutation hooks, native attempts, retry timers and release are distinct work. Frame source admission cannot substitute for native-attempt/debt authority. Committed plus cleanup/release failure cannot be labeled wholly settled; a before mismatch must preserve the actual reported failure/disposition, not manufacture RolledBack.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Actual parent and held propagation
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Private Ready/HeldAtCut/Faulted is appropriately distinct from null, Cancelled, EOF and generic Exception. Shared Stage must branch before preview and must not inject held into existing cleanup catches. Local Ready/Attached does not close the main operation or release a Lost pin. Actual O/I/main/access and join lifetime remain required. No fake ClosedObserved, timeout or metadata fallback is supplied.

source_and_contract_assessments.subject: Liveness, host choice and recoverability limit
source_and_contract_assessments.assessment: Correctly bounded. Client custodian is a conditional hot precondition, not a globally accepted host-mode choice. Original keeper/thread/native owners must survive the same GM-presentation-loss event. Before persisted after-image evidence, a dead keeper loses original entropy; hashes, PID, file absence and new processes cannot restore it. Journal bytes are not a stop/continuation issuer. PF-P05 explicitly lacks a lawful same-action continuation admission, so no successful hot recovery or permanent-HOLD resolution is claimed.
